subject: Skyline - request for breakdown and settlement for retroactive March charges
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena@skyline.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Skyline Finance <finance@skyline.io>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected retro charge on March invoice — request for breakdown

Hi Vivek,

We received the March invoice this morning and there is a one-time retroactive charge labeled 'retro usage adjustment' for $18,720. Our internal billing team says they did not authorize any consumption beyond the committed capacity for March. Can you please provide a line-item breakdown and the raw usage report that triggered this adjustment?

We need enough detail to take to procurement and reconcile on our side — per-model, per-hour, and timestamps if possible. Skyline finance would like to understand whether this is a billing error, a post-term spike, or an after-the-fact measurement.

Thanks,
Elena Morris
Head of Revenue Operations
Skyline Analytics

Attachment: usage_report_march.csv (referenced)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena@skyline.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, Skyline Finance <finance@skyline.io>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2026 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected retro charge on March invoice — request for breakdown

Elena — thanks for flagging and sorry for the surprise. I pulled this into our billing queue and asked Ben and Laura to run the usage reconciliation.

Immediate next steps:
- Ben: run per-model telemetry for the March 1–31 window and validate the aggregation pipeline.
- Laura: review contract commits and confirm whether March had any agreed burst allowances or limits we missed.
- Priya: if this is a customer-exposed credit, please prepare a proposed credit and a note on how it impacts renewal math.

Elena, I attached the raw CSV export our billing system generated for the March window to give you a starting point. We should have an initial write-up by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachment: usage_report_march.csv (sent)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, Elena Morris <elena@skyline.io>, Skyline Finance <finance@skyline.io>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected retro charge on March invoice — initial findings

Team / Elena — quick summary of what I found after correlating the serving telemetry with the billing aggregator:

- On 2026-03-18 between 02:10–03:45 UTC, Skyline triggered a rare long-sequence batch job (model: open-instruct-45B-fp16) that produced high token counts per request. The runtime recorded ~124k additional inference-hours for that 95-minute window compared with typical daily baselines.
- The batch job was not covered by the burst policy in their contract; it exceeded the committed throughput and did not match any recorded 'burst approval' flag.
- The billing pipeline applied a post-hoc reconciliation job on 2026-04-03 which aggregated the late logs and produced the retroactive adjustment that shows on the March invoice.

Recommendation:
- Technical: provide Skyline a by-hour CSV subset for 2026-03-18 (I attached a short analysis PDF).
- Commercial: offer a one-time goodwill credit of 60% of the retro charge (reduces $18,720 to $7,488 billable) and a 30% discount on a dedicated capacity top-up if they commit to an incremental monthly capacity for the next 6 months.

I think this balances contract enforcement with customer goodwill — their usage pattern looks accidental but borderline. If management signs off, I can prepare the adjusted invoice and credit memo.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: analysis_burst.pdf

From: Elena Morris <elena@skyline.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, Skyline Finance <finance@skyline.io>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected retro charge on March invoice — initial findings

Ben — thank you for the quick analysis and for the per-hour detail. The 03-18 window matches internal engineering activity — we were running a model comparison but it was a misconfigured job (our fault). We appreciate the clear breakdown.

Skyline accepts the goodwill approach in principle. Two asks before sign-off:
1) Please confirm the exact credit amount that will appear on our revised invoice (we need line-level numbers for procurement).
2) Can you issue the adjusted invoice and credit memo, and provide a single link we can share with accounting so they can approve payment soon?

We also need this to be clearly reflected in our renewal — the procurement team will want to avoid similar surprises next term and are evaluating a formal dedicated capacity top-up. We are open to the 6-month top-up with the 30% discount; please include the uplift pricing.

Thanks,
Elena

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena@skyline.io>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, Skyline Finance <finance@skyline.io>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2026 11:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected retro charge on March invoice — settlement details and invoice link

Elena — FYI and next steps from the finance side.

- Final agreed credit: 60% of $18,720 = $11,232 credit. Revised charge: $7,488.
- We will re-issue the March adjusted invoice showing the original charge, the credit memo, and the net payable.
- Invoice link (live): https://redwood.app/invoices/INV-2026-03-5643
- DocuSign for settlement approval (one-click acceptance): https://docusign.net/signerlink/AB12C34

If Skyline e-signs the DocuSign and the accounting team confirms the net charge, we'll post the credit memo to your account and issue the updated invoice PDF (attached).

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: adjusted_invoice_2026-03.pdf

From: Skyline Finance <finance@skyline.io>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Elena Morris <elena@skyline.io>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected retro charge on March invoice — settlement confirmed

Laura / Vivek — Skyline finance here. We have e-signed the DocuSign and confirmed the net charge of $7,488. Payment will be processed on the next vendor pay run (scheduled for 2026-05-11). Please confirm the invoice will be moved to 'paid' when the payment settles and that the account portal shows the credit memo immediately.

Also, procurement asked for a written note summarizing the agreed top-up offer (6 months, 30% discount) to include with our renewal packet. Can someone on the Redwood team draft a short commercial summary?

Thanks,
Skyline Finance (on behalf of Skyline Analytics)

Attachment: docusign_settlement_visa.pdf
